result:
**I'd eliminate forced scarcity—making sure no one on Earth lacks the basics to live a dignified life (clean water, nutritious food, shelter, healthcare, and education).**

Not through some magical utopia or by removing all challenge, but by removing the artificial, unnecessary barriers that currently keep billions trapped in survival mode. The world already produces more than enough resources; the problem is how cruelly and inefficiently we distribute them, and how much of human potential is wasted on just staying alive.

If that one change happened, I think almost everything else we argue about—crime, mental health, environmental destruction, even a lot of conflict—would improve dramatically as a side effect. People who aren't desperate tend to be more creative, kinder, and more willing to think long-term.

Everything else I'd want (more curiosity, less tribalism, better incentives for truth-seeking) feels downstream of that one fix.
